prob-parking-lot.title: Design a Multi-Floor Parking Lot
prob-parking-lot.description:
Design an automated parking lot management system for a multi-story commercial complex.

### Functional Requirements:
1. Support multiple floors, each with designated spot types: Compact, Large, Handicapped, and Electric Vehicle (EV) charging spots.
2. Support distinct vehicle types (Motorcycle, Car, Van, Bus, Truck, EV) with physical dimension mapping (e.g. Bus requires multiple consecutive Large spots or designated oversized bay).
3. Automated entry ticketing: Assign optimal available spot nearest to the entrance gate using a dynamic allocation policy.
4. Real-time display boards at each floor entrance showing remaining capacity per spot type.
5. Exit processing and fee calculation based on parking duration, vehicle type, and optional premium EV charging services.
6. Support multiple payment modes (Cash, Credit Card, UPI, Mobile Wallet).

### Concurrency & Non-Functional Requirements:
- Prevent race conditions when two vehicles attempt to claim the last available spot simultaneously.
- Clean object-oriented model separating domain entities, allocation algorithms, and payment processors.
futureRequirements: Change Test A: Add VIP / Reserved corporate parking spots with priority reservation, dynamic surge pricing during peak hours, and penalty rates for unauthorized overstay.
Change Test B: Support license plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that eliminate physical paper tickets and automatically invoice registered accounts upon exit.

prob-elevator-system.title: Design an Intelligent Elevator System
prob-elevator-system.description:
Design a centralized dispatching controller for a bank of 6 high-speed elevators in a 40-floor commercial skyscraper.

### Functional Requirements:
1. Elevators have states: IDLE, MOVING_UP, MOVING_DOWN, MAINTENANCE.
2. Elevators have physical capacities (weight limit and maximum passengers) and door safety sensor interlocks.
3. External Hall Calls: Passengers press Up or Down buttons on any floor.
4. Internal Car Calls: Passengers inside an elevator car select their destination floors.
5. Dispatching Algorithm: Central controller dispatches the most optimal elevator car to minimize passenger wait time and energy consumption (e.g., SCAN, LOOK, or destination dispatching).
6. Emergency handling: Fire alarms immediately lock elevators to ground floor with doors held open; seismic sensors halt cars at nearest floor.

### Constraints:
- Fast scheduling response (< 100ms calculation).
- Graceful degradation if 1 or 2 cars undergo maintenance.
futureRequirements: Change Test A: Implement Destination Dispatching where passengers input their destination floor at a kiosk outside the elevator lobby before boarding, and the system groups passengers going to proximate floors.
Change Test B: Implement Peak-Hour Zone Partitioning (e.g. Elevators 1-2 serve floors 1-15, Elevators 3-4 serve 16-30, Elevators 5-6 serve 31-40 express).

prob-vending-machine.title: Design a State-Driven Vending Machine
prob-vending-machine.description:
Design a standalone automated vending machine serving snacks and cold beverages.

### Functional Requirements:
1. Inventory Management: Machine holds items across multiple slots (aisles), each with rack capacity, item code, price, and stock count.
2. Lifecycle States: Machine operates through distinct states (NoCoinInserted, HasCoin/MoneyAccumulated, ProductSelected, DispensingProduct, RefundingChange).
3. Transaction flow:
   - User inserts coins/notes (accepted denominations: $1, $2, $5, $10).
   - User selects an item by slot code.
   - Machine checks price vs accumulated balance, validates stock availability.
   - If balance sufficient, dispenses item and computes exact change.
   - If user cancels transaction, returns all inserted money.
4. Maintenance / Admin mode: Operator can restock inventory, extract collected cash, and update item prices.

### Constraints:
- Prevent illegal state transitions (e.g. cannot dispense item before payment; cannot refund after item has dispensed).
futureRequirements: Change Test A: Add contactless NFC card and QR code payments with external payment gateway integration and transaction authorization timeouts.
Change Test B: Support combo deals and dynamic multi-item basket purchases with discount coupon redemption.

prob-library-management.title: Design a University Library Management System
prob-library-management.description:
Design a digital catalog and lending management system for a university library with over 100,000 titles and physical assets.

### Functional Requirements:
1. Book item modeling: Distinguish between Book (abstract title, author, ISBN, subject) and BookItem (physical copy with barcode, rack location, condition status: AVAILABLE, RESERVED, LOANED, LOST).
2. Member types: Student (max 5 books, 14-day checkout) vs Faculty (max 15 books, 60-day checkout).
3. Search and Discovery: Support multi-criteria searching by Title, Author, Subject, Publication Date, and ISBN.
4. Lending & Circulation:
   - Checkout book copy with automatic due date computation.
   - Return processing with automated fine calculation ($0.50/day overdue).
   - Book reservation queue when all physical copies are on loan.
   - Renewals allowed once if no other member has placed a reservation hold.
5. Notification service: Send email/SMS alerts for upcoming due dates, overdue fines, and reservation arrival.
futureRequirements: Change Test A: Support Digital E-Books and Audiobooks with concurrent lending limits, digital rights management (DRM) download tokens, and auto-return on expiration.
Change Test B: Integrate Inter-Library Loan (ILL) protocol to borrow books from partner universities when out of local stock.

prob-splitwise-expense.title: Design an Expense Sharing System (Splitwise)
prob-splitwise-expense.description:
Design a collaborative expense sharing and debt simplification engine for groups and individuals.

### Functional Requirements:
1. User and Group Management: Users can create private groups, invite members, and track non-group direct 1:1 balances.
2. Add Expense: Support multiple expense split modes:
   - EQUAL: Split evenly among participants (handle odd penny rounding cleanly).
   - EXACT: Explicit monetary amounts specified per user (must sum to total expense).
   - PERCENTAGE: Percentage distribution per user (must sum to 100%).
   - SHARES: Relative proportion distribution (e.g. 2 shares vs 1 share).
3. Balance Sheet & Ledger: For any user, view net balance across all friends and specific group balance sheets.
4. Debt Simplification (Minimizing Cash Flow Transactions):
   - Given a network of directed debts (e.g., A owes B $10, B owes C $10), automatically compute the minimal number of settlement transactions (A pays C $10).
5. Settle Up: Record direct payments between two users to reconcile balances.
futureRequirements: Change Test A: Multi-Currency support with dynamic foreign exchange rate conversion at the timestamp of the expense and currency-hedged settlement.
Change Test B: Recurring monthly subscriptions with automated itemized pro-rata splitting and automated payment reminder webhooks.

content.assumptions: Single standalone machine instance, no distributed/multi-machine sync required for this scope. Coarse-grained locking assumed at the VendingMachine facade level so concurrent coin-insertion and admin operations don't race — full thread-safety internals are out of scope for this design pass. Persistence is in-memory only; inventory and cash register state live in process memory, with admin actions (restock, cash extraction) logged for audit but not durably persisted. Accepted denominations are fixed at $1/$2/$5/$10, and change reserve is assumed unlimited (no "exact change only" edge case) for this MVP. Physical hardware (coin sensors, dispensing motors) is abstracted behind interfaces and out of scope. Expected scale: single retail kiosk, tens of transactions per hour, not a concurrent multi-user terminal.
content.classesAndResponsibilities:
VendingMachine (Context/Facade) — owns Inventory, CashRegister, and the current VendingState; delegates every customer action (insertCoin, selectItem, dispense, cancel) to the current state. Single entry point for UI and admin layers.
VendingState (interface) — declares insertCoin(), selectItem(), dispense(), cancelTransaction(), refund(). Each concrete state implements only the transitions valid from it; anything else throws IllegalStateTransitionException.
NoCoinInsertedState, HasCoinState, ProductSelectedState, DispensingState, RefundingState — concrete states, each responsible only for what's legal in that state.
Inventory — owns a collection of Slot; responsible for stock lookup/decrement only, knows nothing about money.
Slot — value object: slotCode, item, capacity, currentStock, price; owns only its own stock bookkeeping.
Item — value object: itemCode, name, price.
CashRegister — tracks accumulated balance from accepted denominations, computes exact change via ChangeCalculator; knows nothing about inventory.
ChangeCalculator — pure strategy that computes minimal-denomination change breakdown, isolated so denomination rules can change independently.
PaymentMethod (interface) + CashPayment (initial implementation) — abstracts how money enters the system.
Transaction — represents one purchase attempt (id, selection, amountInserted, status); created on first coin insert, closed on dispense/refund. This is the audit/history record.
AdminService — separate from the customer state machine entirely; handles restock, cash extraction, price updates directly against Inventory/CashRegister. Different actor, different responsibility, deliberately decoupled from VendingState.
VendingMachineException hierarchy — IllegalStateTransitionException, InsufficientStockException, InsufficientBalanceException for deterministic, specific error signaling.
content.relationships: VendingMachine has-a current VendingState (State pattern) and delegates all customer actions to it; each concrete state references back to VendingMachine through a narrow context interface to trigger legal transitions and read Inventory/CashRegister — VendingMachine itself never knows the internals of any state (Dependency Inversion). VendingMachine has-a Inventory (composition), Inventory has-many Slots (composition — a Slot has no meaning outside an Inventory). VendingMachine has-a CashRegister (composition); CashRegister uses ChangeCalculator (injected dependency, swappable without touching CashRegister's core logic). A Transaction is created when the first coin is inserted (HasCoinState) and referenced through ProductSelectedState/DispensingState for the life of that flow, then closed independently of in-memory state. AdminService depends on Inventory and CashRegister directly but never on VendingState — restocking mid-transaction can't corrupt an active customer flow. PaymentMethod is injected into VendingMachine/HasCoinState (Dependency Injection) rather than hardcoded, so it can be swapped without modifying any state class.
content.extensibilityAnswer:
Change Test A (NFC/QR + external gateway + auth timeouts): Because payment acceptance already sits behind the PaymentMethod interface, NFCPaymentMethod and QRPaymentMethod become new implementations calling a PaymentGatewayClient port — zero changes to existing state classes. Auth timeouts are handled by a TimeoutGuardedPaymentMethod decorator wrapping any PaymentMethod, again without touching VendingState implementations. CashRegister.balance is payment-method-agnostic, so no core class needs modification — this is pure Open/Closed extension via new PaymentMethod implementations.

Change Test B (combo deals, multi-item basket, coupons): Transaction evolves from a single slotCode to a List<LineItem> (slotCode + quantity) — a localized change to Transaction and ProductSelectedState's selection logic, not a state-machine redesign. A new PricingStrategy interface (same shape as PaymentMethod) is introduced — SimplePricing today, ComboPricingStrategy/CouponPricingStrategy later — injected at checkout. CashRegister and Inventory stay untouched since they only deal in "charge this amount" and "decrement this slot," never in how that amount was derived. Because money computation was already isolated from inventory/state logic via SRP, basket support is additive, not a rewrite.

content.assumptions: Machine works fine for one type of item. Should be easy to build.
content.classesAndResponsibilities:
VendingMachine — handles everything: inventory, coins, states, dispensing, admin, pricing, change calculation. Has methods like insertCoin(), selectItem(), dispense(), checkStock(), computeChange(), restock(), updatePrice(), extractCash(), getCurrentState(), setState().
Item — name, price, stock count. Also has a sell() method that directly reduces VendingMachine's balance and stock (accesses VendingMachine internals directly).
Admin — a class with just one method login(), rest of admin logic lives inside VendingMachine itself as if (isAdmin) checks scattered across methods.
content.relationships: VendingMachine holds a currentState as a plain string ("NO_COIN", "HAS_COIN", "DISPENSING" etc.) and every method starts with a big if/else or switch on this string to decide what's allowed — state transition rules are duplicated across insertCoin(), selectItem(), and dispense(). Item objects call back into VendingMachine's public fields directly to update balance and stock (Item depends on VendingMachine, VendingMachine depends on Item — circular). Admin checks are done via a global isAdminMode boolean flag on VendingMachine that any method can flip, so there's no real separation between customer flow and admin flow — restocking mid-transaction can overwrite currentState.
content.extensibilityAnswer: We can add more payment types later by adding more if/else branches in insertCoin() for each new payment type. Combo deals can be handled by adding a special case in selectItem() that checks if multiple items were selected and applies a discount manually. Should be straightforward to add since we can just add more code where needed.

VendingMachine (Context/Facade) — owns Inventory, CashRegister, and the current VendingState; delegates every customer action (insertCoin, selectItem, dispense, cancel) to the current state. Single entry point for UI and admin layers.
VendingState (interface) — declares insertCoin(), selectItem(), dispense(), cancelTransaction(), refund(). Each concrete state implements only the transitions valid from it; anything else throws IllegalStateTransitionException.
NoCoinInsertedState, HasCoinState, ProductSelectedState, DispensingState, RefundingState — concrete states, each responsible only for what's legal in that state.
Inventory — owns a collection of Slot; responsible for stock lookup/decrement only, knows nothing about money.
Slot — value object: slotCode, item, capacity, currentStock, price; owns only its own stock bookkeeping.
Item — value object: itemCode, name, price.
CashRegister — tracks accumulated balance from accepted denominations, computes exact change via ChangeCalculator; knows nothing about inventory.
ChangeCalculator — pure strategy that computes minimal-denomination change breakdown, isolated so denomination rules can change independently.
PaymentMethod (interface) + CashPayment (initial implementation) — abstracts how money enters the system.
Transaction — represents one purchase attempt (id, selection, amountInserted, status); created on first coin insert, closed on dispense/refund. This is the audit/history record.
AdminService — separate from the customer state machine entirely; handles restock, cash extraction, price updates directly against Inventory/CashRegister. Different actor, different responsibility, deliberately decoupled from VendingState.
VendingMachineException hierarchy — IllegalStateTransitionException, InsufficientStockException, InsufficientBalanceException for deterministic, specific error signaling.
contentSnapshot.relationships: VendingMachine has-a current VendingState (State pattern) and delegates all customer actions to it; each concrete state references back to VendingMachine through a narrow context interface to trigger legal transitions and read Inventory/CashRegister — VendingMachine itself never knows the internals of any state (Dependency Inversion). VendingMachine has-a Inventory (composition), Inventory has-many Slots (composition — a Slot has no meaning outside an Inventory). VendingMachine has-a CashRegister (composition); CashRegister uses ChangeCalculator (injected dependency, swappable without touching CashRegister's core logic). A Transaction is created when the first coin is inserted (HasCoinState) and referenced through ProductSelectedState/DispensingState for the life of that flow, then closed independently of in-memory state. AdminService depends on Inventory and CashRegister directly but never on VendingState — restocking mid-transaction can't corrupt an active customer flow. PaymentMethod is injected into VendingMachine/HasCoinState (Dependency Injection) rather than hardcoded, so it can be swapped without modifying any state class.
contentSnapshot.extensibilityAnswer:
Change Test A (NFC/QR + external gateway + auth timeouts): Because payment acceptance already sits behind the PaymentMethod interface, NFCPaymentMethod and QRPaymentMethod become new implementations calling a PaymentGatewayClient port — zero changes to existing state classes. Auth timeouts are handled by a TimeoutGuardedPaymentMethod decorator wrapping any PaymentMethod, again without touching VendingState implementations. CashRegister.balance is payment-method-agnostic, so no core class needs modification — this is pure Open/Closed extension via new PaymentMethod implementations.

Change Test B (combo deals, multi-item basket, coupons): Transaction evolves from a single slotCode to a List<LineItem> (slotCode + quantity) — a localized change to Transaction and ProductSelectedState's selection logic, not a state-machine redesign. A new PricingStrategy interface (same shape as PaymentMethod) is introduced — SimplePricing today, ComboPricingStrategy/CouponPricingStrategy later — injected at checkout. CashRegister and Inventory stay untouched since they only deal in "charge this amount" and "decrement this slot," never in how that amount was derived. Because money computation was already isolated from inventory/state logic via SRP, basket support is additive, not a rewrite.

contentSnapshot.classesAndResponsibilities:
VendingMachine — handles everything: inventory, coins, states, dispensing, admin, pricing, change calculation. Has methods like insertCoin(), selectItem(), dispense(), checkStock(), computeChange(), restock(), updatePrice(), extractCash(), getCurrentState(), setState().
Item — name, price, stock count. Also has a sell() method that directly reduces VendingMachine's balance and stock (accesses VendingMachine internals directly).
Admin — a class with just one method login(), rest of admin logic lives inside VendingMachine itself as if (isAdmin) checks scattered across methods.
contentSnapshot.relationships: VendingMachine holds a currentState as a plain string ("NO_COIN", "HAS_COIN", "DISPENSING" etc.) and every method starts with a big if/else or switch on this string to decide what's allowed — state transition rules are duplicated across insertCoin(), selectItem(), and dispense(). Item objects call back into VendingMachine's public fields directly to update balance and stock (Item depends on VendingMachine, VendingMachine depends on Item — circular). Admin checks are done via a global isAdminMode boolean flag on VendingMachine that any method can flip, so there's no real separation between customer flow and admin flow — restocking mid-transaction can overwrite currentState.
contentSnapshot.extensibilityAnswer: We can add more payment types later by adding more if/else branches in insertCoin() for each new payment type. Combo deals can be handled by adding a special case in selectItem() that checks if multiple items were selected and applies a discount manually. Should be straightforward to add since we can just add more code where needed.
